title: The ten thousand guests within
text: Your body carries roughly as {{1}} bacterial cells as human ones, and for decades medicine treated them all as enemies. {{2}} turns out that they are closer to staff than squatters. They digest fibre, {{3}} would otherwise pass through us untouched, manufacture vitamins, and train the immune system to tell friend from foe. Researchers {{4}} once dismissed the whole idea now speak of the microbiome as an organ in its own right. Imbalances {{5}} these communities have been linked to conditions as varied as obesity, allergies and anxiety, and faecal transplants, once unthinkable, are now used {{6}} treat stubborn infections. Medicine is only beginning to grasp {{7}} much influence these microscopic guests exert. The body, it turns out, is not a sealed fortress {{8}} a bustling ecosystem we share with trillions of companions.

gaps.explanation: Countable plural noun, so the comparison is 'as many … as'.
'It turns out that…' — the dummy subject introduces the revelation.
Non-defining relative after the comma, referring to fibre.
Refers to people; the subject form is 'who'.
Imbalances are located in the communities.
'Are used to treat' — the infinitive of purpose after 'used'.
'How much' measures degree: how much influence.

gaps.hint: conjunction: not a fortress ___ an ecosystem
gaps.explanation: 'Not X but Y' — the contrasting second element takes 'but'.
